author: gokhanagingil
body: ## Why On staging, almost all dashboard cards rendered as zero and several sidebar pages returned `Internal server error`. The shell loaded and login worked, but the operational surface of the amateur platform looked broken to anyone clicking around. Two unrelated problems compounded each other: 1. **A real backend crash** — `FinanceService.buildChargeSummaries` returned each charge with `dueDate` still typed as the raw PostgreSQL date string. Downstream consumers (`ActionCenterService.buildFinanceItems`, `ReportingService.commandCenter`, `AuthService.getPlatformOverview`) called `dueDate.getTime()` on it and threw `TypeError: charge.dueDate.getTime is not a function`. That single bug 500'd `/api/action-center/items`, `/api/reporting/command-center`, and (transitively, via the action-center call inside platform overview) `/api/auth/platform-overview` — i.e. the dashboard's primary data sources. 2. **The base demo seed is intentionally minimal** — 3-5 athletes per club, a couple of charges, one or two attendances. Even with the crash fixed the dashboard would still look empty. Believable demos need an order of magnitude more data, varied across clubs. This PR fixes (1) at the root, adds an idempotent expansion seed for (2), and ships a regression smoke script that walks every sidebar endpoint so this class of failure is caught next time before it reaches staging. ## What changed ### Phase 1 — Backend root-cause fix - `apps/api/src/modules/finance/finance.service.ts`: in `buildChargeSummaries`, include the locally constructed `Date` (`charge.dueDate ? new Date(charge.dueDate) : null`) in the returned row so in-process consumers receive a real `Date` instance. This eliminates the cascade of 500s. ### Phase 3 — Demo data expansion (idempotent) - New file `apps/api/src/database/seed/demo-seed-expansion.ts` runs **after** the existing base demo seed (it does not duplicate, replace, or fork the base seed). Reuses the existing tenant, sport branch, and base charge item rows. - For each of the four demo clubs the expansion deterministically generates: - 22-29 athletes with Turkish synthetic names (active / trial / paused mix), realistic birth years per group, optional jersey numbers, 1-2 guardians per athlete, optional team membership. - 12-21 additional guardians with phone / email / notes variability and three guardian portal invitations per club. - 3-4 extra coaches per club with distinct specialties (one inactive coach in Kadıköy to keep the active-only filter honest). - Additional age groups, club groups, and 1-2 teams per group. - 5-7 weekly recurring training sessions per group, each with seeded attendance (≈78% present, mix of late / excused / absent), plus 3-5 upcoming planned sessions. - 2-4 private lessons per club covering past completed and future planned states. One lesson per club intentionally lacks focus or location so it surfaces in the action center. - Three months of monthly dues per athlete (mix of paid / partially paid / pending / cancelled), plus sprinkled merchandise / tournament / camp charges, with matching payments and allocations. Each club has a different overdue rate so dashboards diverge — Moda ≈22%, Marmara ≈16%, Kadıköy ≈18%, Fesa ≈12%. - All row ids are derived from `stableId(slug, kind, key, …)` SHA-256 → UUID so re-running the seed upserts in place. - The expansion can be skipped with `SKIP_DEMO_SEED_EXPANSION=true` for environments that want only the original smoke seed. - `apps/api/src/database/seed/run-demo-seed.ts` invokes the expansion after the base seed. - `apps/api/src/database/seed/verify-demo-seed-repeatability.ts` now exercises both seed phases and enforces stricter minimums (≥18 athletes, ≥12 guardians, ≥8 sessions, ≥20 charges per club). ### Phase 5 — Smoke test - New `scripts/dashboard-smoke.mjs` plus an `npm run dashboard:smoke` script. The smoke logs in as the global admin and walks every endpoint that powers the staff sidebar across every accessible tenant, asserts that `/api/auth/platform-overview` works for the global admin, and asserts that `/api/reporting/command-center` still has the `stats`, `attendance`, `actionCenter` (with an `items` array), and `familyWorkflow` blocks the dashboard expects. Override `API_BASE`, `ADMIN_EMAIL`, or `ADMIN_PASSWORD` to point it at a different environment. ### Documentation - `docs/bootstrap.md` updated to describe the demo seed expansion (per-club footprint, opt-out flag, where to tune the per-club profile knobs) and the new `npm run dashboard:smoke` command. ## Validation - `npm run lint` — passes with `--max-warnings 0`. - `npm run build` — passes (api + web). - `npm run i18n:check` — passes. - `npm run repo:guard` — passes. - `npm run seed:demo` — succeeds twice in a row; no duplicate rows. - `node dist/database/seed/verify-demo-seed-repeatability.js` — passes; confirms idempotency across two seed cycles for all four clubs at the new stricter minimums. - `npm run dashboard:smoke` — passes against a freshly seeded local API; every sidebar endpoint returns 200 for every accessible tenant for the global admin. - Tenant isolation: a club admin sending `X-Tenant-Id` for another club still receives 403, and a club admin hitting `/api/auth/platform-overview` still receives 403. All 22 sidebar endpoints return 200 for a club admin against their own club. Per-club dashboard snapshot after the fix and seed: | Club | Athletes | Guardians | Coaches | Groups | Teams | Sessions | Charges | Payments | Outstanding (TRY) | Overdue (TRY) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Kadıköy | 27 | 19 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 26 | 88 | 66 | 35,900 | 5,950 | | Fesa | 27 | 20 | 6 | 4 | 3 | 20 | 92 | 72 | 42,250 | 8,600 | | Moda | 22 | 16 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 16 | 68 | 55 | 27,425 | 5,525 | | Marmara | 29 | 21 | 6 | 4 | 3 | 21 | 98 | 75 | 40,625 | 6,875 | Each club has a distinct profile: Marmara has the most attendance volume, Moda has the highest overdue ratio, Kadıköy has the most groups, Fesa has the fewest overdue rows but the largest charge backlog. ## Out of scope / follow-ups - Communication module is intentionally not seeded with sent messages — the controller currently exposes only `audiences`, no message history endpoint to populate against. - Action-center "training prep" and "training attendance" categories will populate as wall-clock time advances against the seeded session timestamps; no extra data needed. - The existing wave-10 notification-center hardening already returns clean empty states for the few categories that have no candidates yet, so no further frontend hardening was needed in this pass.

body:
## Release Summary

Job pipeline overhaul: multi-ATS support, automatic provider detection, stale job cleanup, individual job deletion, mock mode removal, three new ATS provider integrations, a performance pass that took scan runtime from ~48s to ~8s, and new content documenting the work. 11 merged PRs.

---

## PRs Included

### #409 — Stale job detection + delete postings (#402, #403)
- **Stale detection**: After polling each source, compares API IDs against DB rows. Jobs absent from the API are auto-archived. Preserves user-intent statuses (`saved`, `applied`).
- **Delete endpoint**: `DELETE /jobs/{posting_id}` for permanent removal. Proxied through Next.js with confirm dialog in `JobDetail`.
- `archived_jobs` counter added to `PollResult` and `ScanButton` display.

### #410 — Remove mock mode
- Deleted `mockData.ts` (530+ lines) and all mock branches from 6 route files.
- All proxy routes simplified to pure `verifyJobsAdmin()` + `proxyToFastAPI()`.
- 4 test files rewritten to test proxy calls instead of mock behavior.
- **Net: -675 lines.**

### #411 — Verify board token (#404)
- `GET /sources/verify?board_token={slug}` endpoint probes Greenhouse's API to validate a token before adding it.
- Next.js proxy route + SourcesPanel UI with Verify button, auto-fill company name, and valid/invalid badge.
- 5 backend tests (valid, invalid, network error, bad format, auth).

### #412 — Multi-ATS support + auto-detect + crawl research (#405, #406, #407)
**Multi-ATS (#405):**
- `StandardJob` shared dataclass replaces `GreenhouseJob`. `external_id: str` replaces `greenhouse_id: int`.
- New fetchers: `lever.py` (Lever API) and `ashby.py` (Ashby API).
- `FETCHERS` dispatch dict in poller routes each source to its provider's fetcher.
- DB migration: `provider` column on `job_sources`, `external_id` rename, composite unique `(source_id, external_id)`.
- Provider dropdown and badge in SourcesPanel.

**Auto-detect ATS (#406):**
- `ats_detect.py` detection service: parses known ATS URLs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters) or probes providers with a plain slug.
- `GET /sources/detect?q={input}` endpoint + Next.js proxy.
- Redesigned SourcesPanel: single "Company name or careers URL" input with Detect button. Manual entry preserved as collapsible Advanced section.

**Crawl research (#407):**
- Research doc at `.claude/docs/research-407-crawl-tools.md` evaluating 8 crawl/extraction tools.
- Key finding: Workday and SmartRecruiters have free unauthenticated JSON APIs.
- Recommendation: Crawl4AI (free, Python-native) for Tier 3 fallback.

### #418 — Workday, SmartRecruiters, and JSON-LD fetchers (#415, #416, #417)
- **Workday** (#415): Pipe-delimited token format (`base_url|tenant|site`), fetches from `/wday/cxs/` internal JSON API with pagination.
- **SmartRecruiters** (#416): Public Posting API v1 (`/v1/companies/{id}/postings`).
- **JSON-LD** (#417): Extracts `schema.org/JobPosting` structured data from any careers page using Python stdlib `html.parser` — handles single objects, arrays, and `@graph` format. Zero new dependencies.
- SmartRecruiters added to auto-detect probing. Workday URL pattern added to `_parse_input`.
- `board_token` pattern relaxed to `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.:/|@-]{1,250}$` for URLs and compound tokens.
- Frontend `PROVIDERS` array updated with all three new providers.

### #419 — Concurrent polling + US-only location filter
- Sources now polled concurrently via `asyncio.gather` with a `POLL_CONCURRENCY=10` semaphore instead of the previous sequential loop.
- `_is_us_location` rejects postings whose location contains a known non-US country or major city name (~90 substrings). Empty locations and generic "Remote" pass through, since many US companies list remote roles without a country.
- `_poll_one_source` refactored out of `poll_all_sources` so per-source errors stay scoped.
- 13 new unit tests for the location filter.

### #420 — Batch Supabase writes in poller, seed, and delete
- Collapsed N+1 write patterns in the three job-api hot paths:
  - Poller: one bulk upsert per source + one `.in_()` archive update (was one round trip per job).
  - `sources.seed_sources`: single bulk upsert of `COMPANY_SEED` (was per-company).
  - `jobs.delete_job`: dropped the pre-SELECT; 404 check reads from the delete response.
- Cut scan runtime from ~48s to ~22s.

### #421 — Offload blocking Supabase calls to thread pool
- Wrapped every `.execute()` in the poller in `asyncio.to_thread(...)` so `supabase-py`'s sync client stops blocking the event loop.
- Combined with `POLL_CONCURRENCY=10`, DB round trips now actually overlap across sources instead of serializing on the single event loop thread.
- Cut scan runtime from ~22s to ~8s.

### #422 — Content: async performance post + expanded job pipeline case study
- New blog post `asyncio-gather-sync-client.mdx` walking through the three fixes from #419 → #420 → #421 and why concurrent polling alone did not help when the Supabase client was sync.
- Expanded the `job-pipeline-case-study` project page from the original single-ATS Greenhouse write-up to the current six-provider pipeline: Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, and a JSON-LD stdlib fallback, plus the auto-detect input and the 8-second scan button.
- Flagged the project update with a dated note at the top of the body so readers can tell the case study was refreshed.
- Wired through `blog.ts`, `content/blog/index.ts`, `contentOrder.ts`; content registry test counts bumped (blogs 40→41, total 56→57).

---

## Database Migration

`supabase/migrations/20260416120000_add_source_provider.sql`:
- Adds `provider TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'greenhouse'` to `job_sources`
- Renames `greenhouse_id` → `external_id` on `job_postings`
- Replaces single-column unique with composite `(source_id, external_id)`

**Run `pnpm db:push` after merge.**

---

## Performance Timeline

| Step | Scan runtime |
|---|---|
| Before #419 | ~48s (sequential polling) |
| After #419 (concurrent polling + US filter) | ~48s (DB writes were the real bottleneck) |
| After #420 (batched writes) | ~22s |
| After #421 (thread-pool offload) | **~8s** |

---

## Test Coverage

| Suite | Count | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Python (pytest) | 129 | All pass |
| JS (Jest) | 903 | All pass |
| TypeScript | — | Zero errors |
| Ruff lint | — | Clean |

New test files: `test_lever.py` (5), `test_ashby.py` (4), `test_ats_detect.py` (19), `test_workday.py` (4), `test_smartrecruiters.py` (5), `test_jsonld.py` (12), `test_routers_sources.py` (+14 new), delete tests (3), `test_poller.py` (+13 US-location tests).

---

## Content Added in This Release

- **Blog:** [asyncio-gather-sync-client](apps/root/src/data/content/blog/asyncio-gather-sync-client.mdx) — why `asyncio.gather` alone was not enough for a sync Supabase client, and the three-step fix.
- **Project (updated):** [job-pipeline-case-study](apps/root/src/data/content/projects/job-pipeline-case-study.mdx) — rewritten to cover multi-ATS, auto-detect, and the 48s→8s scan button.

author: tphakala
body:
## Summary

`hlsConsumer.Write` previously handed the caller's `frame.Data` slice header directly to a buffered channel read asynchronously by FFmpeg. Any upstream buffer reuse (for example, when the audiocore router eventually pools its output slices) would race with the FFmpeg reader and corrupt the live audio stream.

This PR copies `frame.Data` once at the top of `Write` so the consumer owns its payload for the lifetime of the channel enqueue. No behaviour change for the live HLS path (still drops oldest frame on channel saturation); cost is one owned copy per frame, orders of magnitude cheaper than the upstream allocations this unblocks pooling for.

Preparation for wiring the existing `buffer.BytePool` / new `Float64Pool` into the audiocore router hot path, which accounts for ~438 GB of 2-day allocation churn in production profiling.

## Test Plan

- [x] New `TestHLSConsumer_WriteDoesNotRetainFrameData` asserts post-Write mutation of the caller's slice is not visible on the channel (fails on main, passes with the fix).
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/api/v2/...` passes.
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/audiocore/... ./internal/analysis/...` passes.
- [x] `golangci-lint run -v` clean.

- Permitir que un admin conecte su cuenta de Mercado Pago vía OAuth y que la app use el `access_token` del admin (no un token global) para crear preferencias y validar pagos.

body:
### Motivation
- Turn the existing Gmail connection from a passive "connected" state into an active Email Operator that helps users save time, spot money risks, and take action from email data.  
- Reuse the existing Gmail OAuth/token storage, Supabase persistence, and finance analysis foundation to build product-grade flows without reworking auth.  
- Keep Gmail access read-only by default and ensure drafts are generated only (no automatic sends) to preserve trust and privacy.  
- Provide a mobile-first, action-oriented UI surface where each button triggers a real backend flow and tracks lightweight product signals.

### Description
- Added a server-side Email Operator module (`src/server/email-operator/`) with separated logic and types: `types.ts`, `summarize.ts`, `urgent.ts`, `subscriptions.ts`, `drafts.ts`, and `digest.ts` implementing scoring, urgent detection, subscription scanning, multi-tone draft generation, and weekly digest composition.  
- Exposed a single production API endpoint `POST /api/integrations/gmail/operator` (`src/app/api/integrations/gmail/operator/route.ts`) which routes actions: `inbox_summary`, `urgent`, `subscriptions`, `draft`, and `digest`, using existing Gmail integration utilities and Supabase user state.  
- Extended `src/lib/integrations/gmail.ts` with typed inbox models and reusable helpers: `GmailInboxMessage`, `fetchInboxMessages`, and `fetchInboxMessageById`, plus parsing helpers so operator flows can fetch metadata without changing OAuth.  
- Upgraded the actions UI: when `?tool=gmail` the `/actions` page becomes an Email Operator surface (`src/app/actions/page.tsx`) with Quick Actions (Summarize Inbox, Show Urgent Emails, Find Subscriptions/Savings, Draft Reply, Weekly Digest), cards for Inbox Summary / Urgent / Subscription Savings / Weekly Digest and a Recent Important Emails section that triggers draft generation (draft only).  
- Instrumentation: added analytics event names to `src/lib/analytics/events.ts` and wired `trackEvent` calls from the Email Operator UI for product signals (`inbox_summary_opened`, `urgent_emails_viewed`, `subscriptions_found`, `savings_action_clicked`, `draft_generated`, `digest_viewed`).

body:
Implements a HACS-compatible Home Assistant custom integration for VIPA / S7 SPEED7 PLCs, communicating via `python-snap7` (replacing unstable `pys7` attempts). One config entry = one HA device, with UI-managed entities stored in `entry.options`.

## Architecture

- **`address.py`** — strict parser for `DB<n>,X<byte>.<bit>` addresses; validates bit index 0–7
- **`plc_client.py`** — thin `snap7.client.Client` wrapper exposing `connect / disconnect / is_connected / read_bool / write_bool / pulse_bool`; catches `RuntimeError` (what snap7 v1.3 actually raises)
- **`coordinator.py`** — `DataUpdateCoordinator` polling binary sensors; auto-reconnects on update failure
- **`config_flow.py`** — config flow validates live PLC connection before saving; options flow supports add binary sensor / add button / list+delete via HA menu steps
- **`binary_sensor.py`** / **`button.py`** — platform implementations; button press triggers `pulse_bool` (write True → sleep → write False) via executor

## Entity config shape (stored in `entry.options`)

```python
# Binary sensor
{"id": "<uuid>", "entity_type": "binary_sensor", "entity_name": "EG Fenster Bad",
 "address": "DB2,X0.0", "device_class": "window", "invert": False}

# Button
{"id": "<uuid>", "entity_type": "button", "entity_name": "Licht Wohnzimmer AN",
 "address": "DB12,X6.0", "pulse_duration_seconds": 0.5}
```

## Scope / non-goals (MVP)
Only `binary_sensor` and `button` entity types. No YAML, no covers/lights/numbers, no TSAP, no non-DB address formats, no batching.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

You are helping to build a new Home Assistant custom integration for a VIPA / S7 PLC that will be distributed as a HACS custom integration.

Goal:
Build a small but meaningful MVP for a Home Assistant custom integration that represents ONE PLC as ONE Home Assistant device, with multiple configurable entities underneath it.

Important context:

* The target PLC is a VIPA CPU 313-5BF13 / SPEED7.
* Existing communication already works reliably from Node-RED to the PLC using:

  * host: 192.168.3.125
  * port: 102
  * rack: 0
  * slot: 2
* Existing Home Assistant integration attempts using pys7 were unstable.
* Therefore, this new integration should use a communication backend that is likely to be more robust with VIPA, preferably `python-snap7`.
* This integration should be built as a proper Home Assistant custom integration with:

  * config flow
  * options flow
  * device registry support
  * entities attached to one PLC device
  * UI-based entity management for an MVP

MVP scope:
Build only the following entity types for now:

1. binary_sensor
2. button

Do NOT implement everything at once.
Do NOT implement covers, lights, numbers, climate, text, or advanced batching yet.
Those can come later.

What the integration should do:

* One config entry = one PLC connection
* One Home Assistant device = one PLC
* Under that device, the user can add multiple entities using a UI
* The UI should support:

  * “Add new binary sensor”
  * “Add new button”
  * editing and deleting existing configured entities
* Entity definitions should be stored in the config entry options

Required connection parameters in config flow:

* name
* host
* port (default 102)
* rack
* slot
* optional poll interval

The config flow must:

* validate the connection to the PLC before saving
* use `python-snap7`
* attempt `client.connect(host, rack, slot, port)` or equivalent correct snap7 usage
* report a user-friendly error if connection fails

The options flow / UI must:

* allow adding entities after the PLC is already configured
* support at least:

  * binary_sensor:

    * name
    * S7 address
    * device_class (optional)
    * invert (boolean)
  * button:

    * name
    * S7 address
    * pulse_duration_seconds (default 0.5)

Supported address format in MVP:

* only support S7 DB bit addresses like:

  * DB2,X0.0
  * DB12,X6.0
* no other address formats yet

Address parser requirements:

* parse strings like `DB12,X6.0`
* extract:

  * db_number = 12
  * byte_index = 6
  * bit_index = 0
* validate invalid addresses cleanly

Communication requirements:

* Use `python-snap7`
* Implement a small PLC client abstraction
* Required methods:

  * connect()
  * disconnect()
  * is_connected()
  * read_bool(address: str) -> bool
  * write_bool(address: str, value: bool)
  * pulse_bool(address: str, duration: float)

Binary sensor behavior:

* poll the configured address on each coordinator update
* publish ON/OFF in Home Assistant
* optionally invert the value if configured

Button behavior:

* when pressed in Home Assistant:

  * write True to the configured bit
  * sleep for pulse_duration_seconds
  * write False
* buttons are for impulse bits only

Home Assistant architecture requirements:

* proper `manifest.json`
* `config_flow.py`
* `__init__.py`
* `const.py`
* `coordinator.py`
* `device_info` so all entities belong to one PLC device
* `binary_sensor.py`
* `button.py`
* `plc_client.py`
* `address.py`
* use DataUpdateCoordinator for polling binary sensors
* store entity definitions in `entry.options`

UI / usability requirements:

* The integration should feel like a real Home Assistant integration
* After adding the PLC, the user should be able to open Options and:

  * add a new binary sensor
  * add a new button
  * see a list of existing configured entities
* It is acceptable in the MVP if entity management in the options flow is simple and list-based
* Use selectors where useful
* Keep the UI understandable and clean

Persistence requirements:

* The PLC connection config is stored in `entry.data`
* Entity configs are stored in `entry.options`
* On reload, entities must be recreated from options

Diagnostics / logging:

* Add useful debug logging for:

  * connect attempts
  * connect success/failure
  * read errors
  * write errors
  * pulse operations
* Keep logs clear and actionable

Initial example entities to test with:

* Binary sensor:

  * name: EG Fenster Bad
  * address: DB2,X0.0
  * device_class: window
* Button:

  * name: Licht Wohnzimmer AN
  * address: DB12,X6.0
  * pulse_duration_seconds: 0.5

These addresses are known-good examples from an existing working setup.

Implementation style:

* clean, modular, production-minded
* do not over-engineer
* prioritize a working MVP
* avoid premature abstraction beyond what is needed
* type hints where useful
* Home Assistant patterns should be followed

Important limitations:

* This is an MVP
* No YAML configuration
* UI-first configuration only
* No automatic import from...

author: cawithhz
body:
### Background
This change continues to refine the `op-info-test` skill around a clearer and more practical workflow for OpInfo-based test authoring:

`dtype discovery -> candidate backfill -> OpInfo validation -> structured failure triage`

At the same time, it keeps the debugging capabilities that are genuinely useful in daily development, but moves them out of the default path and into explicit optional flows.

### Highlights

#### 1. Refactors the main workflow into a probe-first flow
- Adds `workflow/dtype_support_discovery.md`
- Defines the core path as:
  - applicability check
  - PTA-first dtype probe
  - candidate dtype backfill
  - MindSpore OpInfo validation
  - fixed-order failure triage
- Turns dtype discovery into a first-class workflow instead of leaving it as scattered guidance

#### 2. Introduces a reusable dtype probe framework
- Adds `scripts/dtype_probe_execution_framework.py`
- Supports:
  - batch execution across multiple drivers
  - forward/backward dtype probing
  - classification of `unsupported_dtype` vs testcase/tool issues
  - structured JSON / Markdown summaries
- Adds `template/dtype_probe_operator_scaffold.template.py` to make operator-specific probe drivers easier to build

#### 3. Improves probe result credibility
- Introduces `BACKWARD_NOT_APPLICABLE`
- Adds `backward_not_applicable_dtypes` to probe summaries
- Prevents no-grad-path dtypes from being incorrectly counted as `backward_supported_dtypes`
- Tightens unsupported-dtype classification to reduce misclassification of testcase/tool/framework issues as dtype support conclusions

#### 4. Adds lightweight self-check coverage for the probe framework
- Adds `scripts/dtype_probe_framework_selfcheck.py`
- Validates, without requiring a real Ascend/MindSpore runtime:
  - scaffold/framework injection behavior
  - `backward_not_applicable_dtypes` reporting
  - aggregation logic
  - error classification behavior
  - doc-only fallback summary schema
- Provides a lightweight regression guard for future framework changes

#### 5. Strengthens generation constraints for complex `other`-type operators
- Updates `workflow/op_info_generation.md`
- Adds `workflow/other_family_guardrails.md`
- For complex `other` families such as `conv*`, `linear`, `interpolate`, and `normalization/loss`, the skill now explicitly requires:
  - reuse of the nearest family pattern
  - hook completeness checks for wrappers/samples/error/dynamic paths
  - avoidance of one-shot minimal sample generation
- Shifts the strategy from generic synthesis toward structured family-pattern reuse

#### 6. Simplifies the old remote runner design and clarifies remote execution boundaries
- Removes the old:
  - `remote_runner_server.py`
  - `remote_runner_client.py`
  - related remote artifact/template docs
- Adds `workflow/remote_validation_adapter.md`
- Clarifies that a remote machine is only an execution adapter for:
  - running the probe
  - running candidate-backfill validation
  - returning logs and summaries  
  It does **not** decide dtype declarations, testcase scope, or failure ownership.

---

### Additional Improvements

#### 7. Keeps `--count=50`, but moves it into an optional stability stage
- `--count=50` is not removed
- It is now positioned as an **optional post-pass stability round**:
  - after the main validation matrix passes
  - when the user explicitly asks for stability evidence
  - or when the new case looks potentially flaky
- This keeps the default path lightweight while preserving a useful way to catch intermittent failures

#### 8. Restores temporary single-operator isolation for fast iteration
- Reintroduces `workflow/patch_out_old_tests.md`
- Explicitly scopes it as:
  - a temporary debugging/isolation tactic
  - not part of the final repository state
- Supports fast iteration on one newly added operator before restoring the patch and rerunning the full validation matrix

#### 9. Aligns documentation and script-level summary contracts
- `dtype_support_discovery.md` now explicitly documents:
  - `backward_not_applicable_dtypes`
- The probe framework now provides a unified doc-only fallback helper:
  - `build_doc_derived_operator_summary(...)`
- This allows doc-only fallback to emit the same structured summary schema as runtime probing, with:
  - `dtype_declaration_source = doc_derived`

---

### Main Files Changed
- `skills/op-info-test/SKILL.md`
- `skills/op-info-test/workflow/dtype_support_discovery.md`
- `skills/op-info-test/workflow/op_info_generation.md`
- `skills/op-info-test/workflow/other_family_guardrails.md`
- `skills/op-info-test/workflow/patch_out_old_tests.md`
- `skills/op-info-test/workflow/remote_validation_adapter.md`
- `skills/op-info-test/scripts/dtype_probe_execution_framework.py`
- `skills/op-info-test/scripts/dtype_probe_framework_selfcheck.py`
- `skills/op-info-test/template/dtype_probe_operator_scaffold.template.py`

### Current Benefits
- A clearer and more realistic skill workflow for OpInfo authoring
- More trustworthy and interpretable dtype probe results
- Better guardrails for complex `other`-type operators
- Cleaner remote validation boundaries
- Retains high-value developer workflows for fast iteration:
  - temporary single-operator isolation
  - optional `--count=50` stability reruns

### Possible Follow-ups
- Make the scaffold prefer doc-declared candidate dtypes by default, instead of probing the full `DEFAULT_DTYPE_NAMES` set
- If needed, further standardize the command shapes for:
  - targeted temporary isolation runs
  - final full validation runs

## Problem

`HermesA2AExecutor` previously injected tool descriptions as raw text into the system prompt — a fragile workaround that pollutes context, inflates token usage, and bypasses vLLM's native function-calling machinery.

## Solution

Pass tools via the standard OpenAI-compatible `tools=[...]` parameter so the model can use its trained function-calling behavior natively.

## Changes

### `workspace-template/hermes_executor.py`
- `__init__` accepts an optional `tools: list[dict] | None` parameter (copied defensively; `None`/`[]` → empty list)

- Streaming is disabled (`stream=False`) when tools are present, since vLLM doesn't support streaming with function calls (vLLM #31871)
- When the model returns `tool_calls` (non-empty `choice.message.tool_calls`) with no text content, the tool-call objects are serialized as a JSON string and enqueued as an A2A agent text message — preserving the A2A reply contract while carrying full structured data

<!-- opencode-summary-start -->
## Summary

Add webhook notifications for PCSM lifecycle events. Send HTTP POST requests to configured URLs when events like replication failures or finalization completion occur. Supports generic JSON payloads and Slack-formatted messages with configurable event filtering and authentication.
<!-- opencode-summary-end -->

[PCSM-308](https://perconadev.atlassian.net/browse/PCSM-308)

### Problem

PCSM has no way to notify external systems about lifecycle events. Users have to poll the `/status` endpoint to detect state changes like replication failures or finalization completion.

### Solution

Add webhook notifications that send HTTP POST requests to a user-configured URL on key lifecycle events.
Notifications are sent in a fire-and-forget manner.

**New CLI options:**

| Flag | Env Var | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--webhook-url` | `PCSM_WEBHOOK_URL` | Callback URL (required to enable webhooks) |
| `--webhook-events` | `PCSM_WEBHOOK_EVENTS` | Event filter: `all` (default) or `failure` |
| `--webhook-auth-token` | `PCSM_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN` | Bearer token for authentication |
| `--webhook-target` | `PCSM_WEBHOOK_TARGET` | Payload format: `slack` for Slack incoming webhooks |

**Events:** `pcsm:started`, `initial-sync:clone-completed`, `initial-sync:clone-failed`, `initial-sync:completed`, `replication:failed`, `replication:paused`, `replication:resumed`, `finalization:started`,  `finalization:finished`

**Generic payload:**
```json
{
    "event": "replication:failed",
    "timestamp": "2026-04-16T09:08:49Z",
    "message": "change stream error"
}
```

**Slack payload (--webhook-target slack):**
```json
  {
    "text": "*PCSM*\n*Event:* `replication:failed`\n*Message:* change stream error\n*Time:* 2026-04-16T09:08:49Z"
  }
```

[PCSM-308]: https://perconadev.atlassian.net/browse/PCSM-308?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** The API client allowed HTTP connections to external hosts without validation, risking the transmission of unencrypted sensitive data (like authentication tokens and financial data) over the internet.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker intercepting the network traffic could read the `Bearer` token and perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the user, leading to complete account compromise.
🔧 **Fix:** Implemented strict, fail-closed URL parsing. The client now verifies the URL scheme case-insensitively and securely parses the IPv4 hostname. If the scheme is `http`, it ensures the host belongs to a valid local network address (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `10.x.x.x`, `192.168.x.x`, `172.16.x.x-172.31.x.x`). All other external HTTP traffic throws a strict runtime error.
✅ **Verification:** Logic verified via Python isolation testing for IPv4 bounds and constraints to simulate the fail-closed Swift splitting behavior. Local loopback checks correctly pass while attempts to spoof via `10.attacker.com` accurately reject.

body:
# Require origin-country (`jurisdiction`) declaration; enforce USD-only currency

## Summary

Introduces a required `jurisdiction` declaration on every `AppManifest` and
payment/action-tier `ToolManual`, and tightens `currency` to `"USD"` on
`AppManifest` (matching the existing `const "USD"` on `ToolManual`). No
defaults are applied to `jurisdiction` — developers must make an explicit
choice.

**Why now:** a recent platform audit found legacy listings had slipped
through with `currency="JPY"` because neither the SDK nor the registration
endpoint was validating the field. Similarly, without a required
jurisdiction field, every listing implicitly inherited a US default,
which is the kind of invisible decision that causes compliance incidents
later. This PR forces both to be explicit at the earliest possible point
(adapter construction), with the platform as a second enforcement gate.

## Motivation

- **Origin transparency for buyers.** Every API Store listing now renders
  a country-flag icon derived from `jurisdiction`. Buyers see at a glance
  where the API is "from" and can judge fitness for their own jurisdiction
  and use case.
- **Single source of truth on currency.** Stripe Connect destination
  charges, the 93.4% / 6.6% revenue split, and the $5.00/month minimum
  all operate on USD. Non-USD submissions are now rejected at both the
  SDK and the platform.
- **No silent defaults.** Compliance regimes differ by country;
  defaulting to `"US"` when a developer forgot to set the field is worse
  than raising a clear error that forces a decision.

## What's in scope

- `AppManifest.jurisdiction` — **required**, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
  (optionally with sub-region, e.g. `"US-CA"`). No default.
- `AppManifest.currency` — narrowed to the literal `"USD"`. Non-USD
  raises `ValueError` at construction.
- `AppManifest.applicable_regulations` — optional, advisory list (e.g.
  `["GDPR", "CCPA", "資金決済法"]`).
- `AppManifest.data_residency` — optional ISO code for where user data
  is stored; defaults to `jurisdiction` if unset.
- `ToolManual.jurisdiction` — required for `action` / `payment` tiers
  (matches the existing currency/settlement requirement for payment).
- `ToolManual.legal_notes` — optional free-form note surfaced on the
  approval prompt.
- New doc: [`docs/jurisdiction-and-compliance.md`](docs/jurisdiction-and-compliance.md)
  covering the what/why/how including an FX/JP example and flag-icon
  rendering notes.

## Explicitly out of scope

The first draft of this PR also included `served_markets` /
`excluded_markets` / `restriction_reason` — platform-enforced allowlists
and blocklists for buyer countries. These were removed in the final
commit after feedback: whether an API is valid in the buyer's country
is inherently case-by-case (concrete example: a seismic-calculation API
built to US IBC codes is probably not valid for a JP structural engineer
filing under 建築基準法, but may still be useful as a reference or
comparative input — only the buyer knows). The platform surfaces origin
clearly; the buyer judges fitness.

## Breaking changes

- **`AppManifest.jurisdiction` becomes required.** Existing code like
  `AppManifest(capability_key="x", name="X")` now raises `ValueError`.
  Migration: add `jurisdiction="US"` (or your correct origin country).
- **`AppManifest.currency` is now a `"USD"` literal in TS.** Consumers
  passing a variable-typed string may need to narrow. Python rejects
  non-USD at construction.

All four in-tree `examples/` adapters were updated to declare
`jurisdiction="US"` explicitly.

## Validation layering

1. **SDK construction** (`__post_init__` / `to_dict`) — catches
   typos and missing values at adapter build time with a clear message.
2. **JSON schemas** (`schemas/app-manifest.schema.json`,
   `schemas/tool-manual.schema.json`) — `const "USD"` for currency,
   `pattern: ^[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?$` for jurisdiction / data_residency.
3. **Platform registration** — rejects non-USD with
   `CURRENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED` (422) and missing jurisdiction with
   `JURISDICTION_REQUIRED` (422).

## Test plan

- [x] Smoke test: `AppManifest(jurisdiction="US")` accepted
- [x] Smoke test: missing `jurisdiction` raises `ValueError`
- [x] Smoke test: `jurisdiction="us-ca"` lowercase — malformed rejected
- [x] Smoke test: `jurisdiction="US-CA"` sub-region accepted
- [x] Smoke test: `currency="JPY"` raises `ValueError`
- [x] Smoke test: `currency="usd"` normalized to `"USD"`
- [x] Smoke test: `ToolManual` with `permission_class=ACTION` requires
  `jurisdiction` on `to_dict()`
- [x] All four in-tree `examples/` adapters updated to declare
  `jurisdiction` explicitly
- [x] JSON schemas updated and consistent with Python / TS
- [ ] Reviewer check: does any downstream code construct `AppManifest`
  without passing `jurisdiction`? (Search for usages that may need
  migration alongside this PR.)

## Commit layout

Four focused commits for easier review:

1. `Add jurisdiction declaration to AppManifest and ToolManual` — the
   feature addition with the three auxiliary fields.
2. `Enforce USD-only currency on AppManifest` — tightens the currency
   contract that was already `const "USD"` on ToolManual.
3. `Require explicit jurisdiction; add served_markets / excluded_markets` —
   removes the silent US default; introduces the buyer-country
   allowlist/blocklist that commit 4 walks back.
4. `Simplify: jurisdiction is origin-declaration only (buyer judges fitness)` —
   walks back the buyer-country enforcement in favor of origin-declaration
   only.

## Summary

- Adds an `InvestmentWithdrawal` table + matching server, hook, and UI layers so users can record money flowing *out* of investments (parallel to the existing deposit flow).
- **Lump sum / Savings:** partial or full withdrawals — reduce `currentValue` only; `investedAmount` stays intact so ROI math (`currentValue + totalWithdrawn` vs `investedAmount`) stays computable.
- **DPS (scheduled):** a "Close prematurely" action — user enters the amount actually received (often less than accrued value due to bank penalty), the scheme flips to `status='closed'`, all upcoming installments are deleted.
- **ROI fix:** list and detail views now compute return as `(currentValue + totalWithdrawn) / investedAmount`, so partial withdrawals don't appear as losses.
- **Closure UX:** "Mark as closed" only triggers on full withdrawals — prevents silently stranding residual balance.
- Notifications fire for every withdrawal and DPS closure via the existing `createNotification` helper.

## Files of note
- `prisma/schema.prisma` + `prisma/migrations/20260417120000_add_investment_withdrawals/` — new table with cascade on Investment/Profile.
- `src/server/investments.impl.ts` — `withdrawImpl`, `closeDpsImpl`, `totalWithdrawn` aggregation in list, withdrawals included in detail.
- `src/lib/validators.ts` — `withdrawalSchema`, `dpsCloseSchema`.
- `src/hooks/useInvestments.ts` — `useWithdraw`, `useCloseDps`.
- 3 detail screens + the list page get the new affordances and reformat the ROI numerator.

The second commit is unrelated prettier formatting that `npm run check` picked up while working in the same tree — no behavior changes.

- [ ] **Validation:** withdraw amount > currentValue → toast error.

## Summary

- `wifimgr search wireless site "<name-or-id>"` (and `search wired`) now returns every client on the given site when no search text is provided. Previously the command required at least one search term — there was no way to say "just show me everything on this site."
- Fixes the docs/behavior mismatch on the `site` argument: the help text said "site-name" but the code compared the value literally against the vendor site/network ID. Resolution now tries the per-API cache first and falls back to treating the input as a raw ID, so both `site "US-LAB-01"` and `site L_3732358191183298569` work.
- No-args invocation (`wifimgr search wireless` with nothing) now errors with a clear message instead of running an unbounded org-wide scan.

```
wifimgr search wireless site "MX - Av. Ejercito Nacional Mexicano 904"
wifimgr search wireless site L_3732358191183298569
wifimgr search wired site US-LAB-01 json
```

- `parseSearchArgs` rewritten to allow `site` as the first positional arg; `validateSearchArgs` enforces "must have text or site."
- `resolveSearchSiteID` in `cmd/multivendor_search.go` resolves the site arg per-API via `CacheManager.GetSiteIDByName`, with passthrough fallback.
- Meraki's `searchNetworkWirelessClients`/`searchNetworkWiredClients` skip the local `matchesText` filter when text is empty. Extracted `shouldApplyLocalFilter` for clarity and testability.

author: suhang56
body:
## Summary

学 astrbot_plugin_group_chat_enhanced 的 fatigue 机制:bot 连续发言后,累积一个 fatigue score,到达阈值开始按比例 dampen 正向 engagement 信号——像真群友累了会少说话,直到歇够了再恢复。

## Design — Option C hybrid(3-way agent 仲裁结果)

**冲突解决过程:**
- **Planner** 提:加法 penalty `-0.3 * min(1, (score-threshold)/2)`
- **Designer** 提:乘法 dampening `score *= max(0.3, 1-0.15*(fatigue-THRESHOLD))` —— UX 上更"真累了",但打破 ScoreFactors 求和模式
- **Architect 仲裁**:**Option C hybrid** —— additive storage(telemetry),multiplicative math(effect)

**最终 formula**(chat.ts:2115-2133):
```ts
if (this.fatigueSource) {
  const rawFatigueScore = this.fatigueSource.getRawScore(groupId);
  if (rawFatigueScore > FATIGUE_THRESHOLD) {
    const multiplier = Math.max(0.3, 1 - 0.15 * (rawFatigueScore - FATIGUE_THRESHOLD));
    const positiveSum = Object.entries(factors)
      .filter(([k, v]) => k !== 'fatiguePenalty' && v > 0)
      .reduce((s, [, v]) => s + v, 0);
    factors.fatiguePenalty = (multiplier - 1) * positiveSum;
  }
}
```

- `fatiguePenalty` 进 ScoreFactors(reducer `Object.values(factors).reduce` 自动吸收,`_pickChatModel` telemetry 可见)
- Math 是乘法:fatigue=7 时 hot 消息 1.4 → multiplier 0.7 → penalty = -0.42 → final 0.98(mellowed,不封口)
- fatigue=10(深累)时 hot 1.4 → multiplier 0.3 cap → penalty = -0.98 → final 0.42 < chatMinScore 0.45 → **silenced**(真睡了)
- **direct trigger**(@ / reply-to-bot)在 chat.ts:1998 short-circuit 前 bypass,fatigue 不阻塞被召唤

## 参数

- `FATIGUE_PER_REPLY = 1.0`(每条 reply +1)
- `FATIGUE_THRESHOLD = 4`(Designer 建议 5→4,Architect 采纳)
- `TAU_MS = (30 * 60_000) / Math.LN2` — **true 30-min half-life**(Architect Option A:Planner 原注释"30min 半衰期"数学对应 TAU/ln2)
- Multiplier 下限 0.3(never silence 超 70%,让 fatigue 只 mellow 不硬 cap)

## 文件 + 架构

- `src/modules/fatigue.ts` 新模块,`BoundedMap(200)` state,没 DB 持久化(bot 重启重置 = 真群友睡觉)
- setter injection pattern(`setFatigueSource`)与 M6.2a/b 一致
- `IFatigueSource` 接口:`onReply` + `getRawScore` + `getPenalty`(两个 read 方法分工:raw 给 hybrid math,penalty 给 unit test)
- Lazy decay(`exp(-dt/TAU)`),无 setInterval,无 timer 泄漏风险

## 5-agent gate

- **Planner** full spec
- **Designer**:no copy needed;建议 THRESHOLD 4 + 乘法数学 + skip `/bot_status` tamagotchi trap
- **Architect**:仲裁 Designer 冲突,设计 hybrid formula,核 ScoreFactors 4 sync sites
- **Developer**:`891d10f` 实现(force-pushed 覆盖初版加法)
- **Reviewer**:独立验证 2121/2/2123,math paper check,短路 invariant 保全

## 测试

- 21 new test(14 unit in `fatigue.test.ts` + 7 integration in `chat-fatigue-wiring.test.ts`)
- Architect 指定的 6 case 全过:
  - (a) 5× onReply + hot → fatiguePenalty<0, sum<positive
  - (b) 10× onReply + hot → sum<chatMinScore 0.45 → skip
  - (c) direct @bot at fatigue=10 → short-circuit bypass,fatiguePenalty=0
  - (d) 未 setFatigueSource → fatiguePenalty=0(backward compat)
  - (e) fatigue=10 + 零正向 factors → fatiguePenalty=0((mult-1)*0)
  - (f) fatigue=threshold 刚好 → fatiguePenalty=0(不过门槛)
- 2 条 pre-existing fail 同 master(metaIdentityProbe + lore identity-core)

## Roadmap

**M6.3 shipped。** 下一件按顺序:
- M6.4 consecutive-reply cap(bot 连说 N 条没人打断 → 硬闭嘴一轮)
- M6.5 relationship → addressing(M6.2a 已部分实现,revisit)
- M6.6 self-reflection → persona patch(人审回路)
- M7-9 roadmap

## Non-blocking followups

- positiveSum filter inline comment(architect nit)—— 下版顺手
- `sev5 kicks` test 3015ms wall-time retrofit(retroreview-pr4 legacy)

body:
## Problem

After a model finishes downloading, `instances` and `runners` remain empty until the user manually calls `POST /place_instance`. The dashboard stays blank and inference is unavailable after every restart or fresh download — requiring a manual step that is easy to forget.

## Solution

In `_event_processor`, after applying a `NodeDownloadProgress` event that transitions to `DownloadCompleted`, the master now automatically issues a `PlaceInstance` with sensible defaults (Pipeline sharding, MlxRing, `min_nodes=1`) — but only if no instance for that model already exists.

The logic is extracted into `_auto_place_on_download_completed` to keep `_event_processor` readable. It reuses the existing `place_instance()` and `get_transition_events()` — no new placement logic is introduced.

## Behaviour

- Fresh download completes → instance appears in dashboard automatically
- Existing instance for a model → no duplicate placement
- Placement failure (e.g. insufficient memory) → logged and skipped silently, same as a failed manual `POST /place_instance`

## Test

Start EXO, trigger a model download, observe that the instance appears in `/state` and the dashboard without any manual `POST /place_instance` call.

author: rorychatt
body:
## Problem

The `EventRegistry` uses `(String, String)` keys for `(widget_id, event_name)`. Event names like `"click"` and `"change"` are passed as bare string literals throughout the codebase. This is error-prone — a typo like `"Click"` instead of `"click"` would silently fail to dispatch.

## Solution

- Added a typed `EventName` enum (`Click`, `Change`) with `as_str()`, `from_str()`, and `Display` implementations
- Added `register_typed()` and `dispatch_typed()` methods to `EventRegistry` for compile-time safe event handling
- Simplified `AppSessionStore` to return owned `AppSession` instead of `Arc<RwLock<AppSession>>`, removing unnecessary shared ownership and the shutdown broadcast channel
- Streamlined WebSocket handler in `ws.rs` to use the owned session directly

### Commits
- `5114eec` — [00223] Add typed EventName enum to event registry

author: pinges
body:
## PR description

  - Remove the legacy pre-EIP-8 (V1) RLPx handshake format, keeping only EIP-8 (V4)
  - Delete InitiatorHandshakeMessageV1, ResponderHandshakeMessageV1, and the V1 encryptMsg/decryptMsg methods from EncryptedMessage

  Motivation

  EIP-8 was introduced with the Homestead hard fork in March 2016. Geth https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22899, noting that no actively maintained client sends this  format. Nethermind, Erigon, and Reth all only support EIP-8. Besu was the last major client still carrying this dead code path.

  Removing V1 simplifies the handshake logic — the ECIESHandshaker no longer needs the version4 flag, the try-V4-then-fallback-to-V1 decryption dance, or the V1 message classes.  The EIP-8 size-prefix framing is now assumed unconditionally.

## Summary

- Server mutations via `POST /api/references/` are now persisted to `library.json`.
- Shutdown (SIGINT / SIGTERM) flushes the in-memory library to disk before closing the file watcher, so ad-hoc in-memory changes (e.g. those made by the direct `library.add` path) survive a stop.
- `ref server stop` now sends `SIGTERM` to the running server instead of only removing the portfile, so the shutdown handler actually runs and the process exits.

Closes #93.

## Root cause

| Route / Path | Operation | `save()` called before? | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST `/api/references/` | `library.add()` direct | No | Yes |
| Shutdown (SIGINT/SIGTERM) | cleanup handler | No | Yes (via `dispose()`) |
| `server stop` | portfile removal only | — | Sends `SIGTERM` first |
